story_description: Users launching Blaze for the first time need guided onboarding that detects installed AI CLIs, offers one-click installation for missing ones, and configures the environment automatically so they can start coding immediately.
task_description: Implement the Skills Recommendations Screen that displays a grid of skill cards fetched from a remote registry, filtered by installed CLIs, with search and category filtering, checkbox selection, and navigation controls for skip and next actions.
atom: Skills Recommendations Screen with Remote Registry Integration
atom_description: A SwiftUI view presenting a searchable, filterable grid of skill cards populated from a remote JSON registry, dynamically filtered to show only skills compatible with the user's detected CLIs, supporting multi-select checkbox behavior, category filtering, popularity sorting, and navigation via Skip and Next buttons.
problem_statement: Users new to AI CLI tools may not know which skills (pre-built prompts, workflows, and configurations) are available or would benefit their workflow. Without curated recommendations filtered to their installed CLIs, users must manually discover and configure skills, reducing time-to-value and increasing onboarding friction.
scope_in: Fetch skill metadata from remote registry endpoint (JSON over HTTPS)
Parse skill registry response into local SkillCard models with id, name, description, category, for_cli array, stars count, downloads count, and recommended flag
Display skills in a responsive grid layout with 2-3 columns based on window width
Filter displayed skills to only those matching at least one installed CLI from previous detection screen
Implement text search filtering across skill name and description fields
Implement category filter dropdown with All plus unique categories from registry
Sort skills by popularity using weighted score of stars and downloads
Display Recommended badge on skills flagged as recommended in registry
Implement checkbox selection state for each skill card with visual feedback
Track selected skills in view model for later installation
Provide Skip button that navigates forward without selecting any skills
Provide Next button that navigates forward and queues selected skills for installation
Show loading state while fetching registry data
Show error state with retry option if registry fetch fails
Cache registry response locally to avoid refetch on back navigation
scope_out: Actual skill installation logic - deferred to completion screen batch install
Skill preview or detailed view modal - users see name, description, and badges only
User-uploaded or custom skills - only registry-hosted skills shown
Skill version management or updates - initial install only
Offline skill bundle fallback - requires network for registry fetch
Skill dependency resolution - skills are independent units
Rating or review submission - read-only popularity metrics
assumptions: Remote skills registry is hosted at a stable HTTPS endpoint returning valid JSON
Registry schema includes for_cli field as array of CLI identifiers matching SupportedCLI enum rawValues
Previous onboarding screen (CLI detection) has populated OnboardingState.detectedCLIs array
Network is available during onboarding flow (same assumption as CLI installation)
Registry response is reasonably sized (under 1MB, under 500 skills)
Category values in registry are consistent strings suitable for grouping
constraints: Must not block main thread during network fetch or JSON parsing
Must complete registry fetch and initial render within 5 seconds on typical network
Must handle registry unavailability gracefully with informative error state
Must preserve selection state if user navigates back and forward
Must support VoiceOver accessibility for all interactive elements
Must work with zero installed CLIs by showing empty state with guidance message
Grid layout must be responsive from 800px to 1600px window widths
functional_requirements: FR1: On view appear, fetch skills registry from configured HTTPS endpoint using URLSession
FR2: Parse registry JSON response into array of SkillCard models with validation for required fields
FR3: Filter skills array to include only skills where for_cli array intersects with OnboardingState.detectedCLIs
FR4: Display filtered skills in a LazyVGrid with adaptive column sizing (minimum 280pt per card)
FR5: Each skill card shows name, truncated description (2 lines), category badge, star count, download count, Recommended badge if flagged, and selection checkbox
FR6: Implement search TextField that filters displayed skills by case-insensitive substring match on name or description
FR7: Implement category Picker that filters displayed skills by exact category match, with All option to show all
FR8: Sort displayed skills by popularity score calculated as (stars * 2) + downloads, descending
FR9: Checkbox tap toggles selection state for that skill and updates selectedSkills set in view model
FR10: Display count of selected skills in header area (e.g., 3 skills selected)
FR11: Skip button is always enabled and navigates to next onboarding screen without queuing any skills
FR12: Next button is always enabled (unlike CLI screen), navigates forward, and persists selectedSkills to OnboardingState
FR13: Show loading skeleton grid while registry fetch is in progress
FR14: Show error view with message and Retry button if registry fetch fails
FR15: Cache successful registry response in memory for session duration to handle back navigation
nonfunctional_requirements: NFR1: Registry fetch completes within 5 seconds or times out with error state
NFR2: JSON parsing and filtering complete within 100ms for up to 500 skills
NFR3: Grid renders at 60fps during scroll with no frame drops
NFR4: Memory usage for skill cards stays under 30MB for 500 skills
NFR5: VoiceOver announces skill name, category, selection state, and badge status correctly
NFR6: Search and filter operations complete within 50ms with no perceived lag
implementation_steps: Step 1: Create SkillsRecommendationsView.swift with @StateObject for SkillsRecommendationsViewModel

Step 2: Define SkillCard model struct conforming to Identifiable, Codable with fields: id (String), name (String), description (String), category (String), forCLIs ([String]), stars (Int), downloads (Int), isRecommended (Bool)
Step 3: Define SkillsRegistryResponse struct conforming to Codable wrapping array of SkillCard
Step 4: Create SkillsRecommendationsViewModel with Published properties: allSkills, filteredSkills, selectedSkillIDs, searchText, selectedCategory, loadingState
Step 5: Define LoadingState enum: idle, loading, loaded, error(String)
Step 6: Implement fetchRegistry async method using URLSession.shared.data(from:) with 5-second timeout configuration
Step 7: Implement parseRegistry method that decodes JSON and validates required fields
Step 8: Implement filterSkillsByCLI method that filters allSkills based on OnboardingState.detectedCLIs intersection
Step 9: Implement applyFilters method that chains CLI filter, search filter, category filter, and popularity sort
Step 10: Add Combine pipeline using Publishers.CombineLatest3 for searchText, selectedCategory, allSkills to trigger applyFilters
Step 11: Implement popularityScore computed property on SkillCard returning (stars * 2) + downloads
Step 12: Create SkillCardView subview with card background, name label, description text (lineLimit 2), category badge, stats row, recommended badge, and checkbox
Step 13: Implement checkbox toggle binding that adds/removes skill ID from selectedSkillIDs set
Step 14: Build header section with search TextField, category Picker, and selection count label
Step 15: Build main content with LazyVGrid using adaptive GridItem with minimum 280pt
Step 16: Create LoadingSkeletonGrid view showing 6 placeholder cards with shimmer animation
Step 17: Create ErrorStateView with error message and Retry button that calls fetchRegistry
Step 18: Create EmptyStateView for case when no skills match filters or no CLIs detected
Step 19: Wire Skip button to OnboardingCoordinator.advance() without modifying state
Step 20: Wire Next button to persist selectedSkillIDs to OnboardingState.selectedSkills then OnboardingCoordinator.advance()
Step 21: Add onAppear modifier to trigger fetchRegistry if loadingState is idle
Step 22: Implement registry response caching in view model to preserve data on back navigation
Step 23: Add telemetry calls for screen viewed, search performed, category changed, skills selected, skip pressed, next pressed
Step 24: Write unit tests for filtering logic, sorting logic, and selection state management
Step 25: Write UI tests for search interaction, category filtering, card selection, and navigation
data_model_changes: Add SkillCard struct: id (String), name (String), description (String), category (String), forCLIs ([String]), stars (Int), downloads (Int), isRecommended (Bool), conforming to Identifiable, Codable, Hashable
Add SkillsRegistryResponse struct: skills ([SkillCard]), version (String), updatedAt (String), conforming to Codable
Add LoadingState enum: idle, loading, loaded, error(String)
Extend OnboardingState with selectedSkills: Set<String> for persisting selected skill IDs across navigation
api_contracts: GET https://registry.blaze.app/v1/skills -> SkillsRegistryResponse JSON with 200 OK or error status
SkillsRegistryService.fetchSkills() async throws -> [SkillCard] encapsulating network call and parsing
event_contracts: OnboardingEvent.skillsScreenViewed - emitted when view appears with detected CLI count
OnboardingEvent.skillsRegistryFetchCompleted(count: Int) - emitted with number of skills loaded
OnboardingEvent.skillsSearchPerformed(query: String, resultCount: Int) - emitted on search with results
OnboardingEvent.skillsCategoryChanged(category: String, resultCount: Int) - emitted on category filter change
OnboardingEvent.skillSelected(skillId: String) - emitted when skill checkbox checked
OnboardingEvent.skillDeselected(skillId: String) - emitted when skill checkbox unchecked
OnboardingEvent.skillsScreenSkipped - emitted when Skip button pressed
OnboardingEvent.skillsScreenCompleted(selectedCount: Int) - emitted when Next button pressed with selection count
ui_states: Loading state: Skeleton grid with 6 shimmer placeholder cards while fetching registry
Loaded state: Grid of skill cards with search bar, category picker, and selection count header
Empty state (no matches): Message explaining no skills match current filters with suggestion to clear filters
Empty state (no CLIs): Message explaining skills require CLI detection first with Back button
Error state: Error message with Retry button centered in content area
Selected state: Skill cards show filled checkbox and highlighted border when selected
ui_interactions: Type in search TextField to filter skills by name or description substring match
Select category from Picker dropdown to filter skills by category
Tap skill card checkbox to toggle selection state
Tap skill card anywhere (not checkbox) to toggle selection state (convenience)
Tap Skip button to proceed without selecting skills
Tap Next button to proceed with selected skills queued for installation
Tap Retry button in error state to re-attempt registry fetch
Scroll grid vertically to view all filtered skills
ui_copy: Try different keywords or clear filters
Skills require at least one CLI to be detected. Go back to install a CLI.
edge_cases: Registry returns empty skills array - show empty state with message that no skills are available yet
All skills are for CLIs user does not have installed - show empty state with guidance to install more CLIs
User has zero detected CLIs - show specialized empty state with back navigation suggestion
Registry returns malformed JSON - parse error handled as fetch error with retry option
Network request times out - show timeout-specific error message
User rapidly toggles same checkbox - debounce or ensure state consistency
Search query matches no skills - show no matches state with clear suggestion
User types very long search query - truncate display but use full query for filtering
Registry returns skill with missing required field - skip that skill with warning log rather than failing entire parse
User navigates back then forward - preserve cached registry data and selection state
failure_modes: Network unreachable during fetch - show error state with offline-specific messaging if detectable
Registry endpoint returns 500 - show server error message with retry option
Registry endpoint returns 404 - show configuration error message and log for investigation
JSON decode fails - show parse error message and log raw response for debugging
Memory pressure during large registry parse - handle gracefully with reduced parsing or pagination
View model deallocated during async fetch - use weak self capture to prevent crashes
Combine pipeline memory leak - ensure proper cancellable storage and cleanup
rollback_plan: If Skills screen proves problematic, it can be bypassed by setting OnboardingState.skipSkillsScreen = true which causes OnboardingCoordinator to skip this step. Selected skills are only persisted to OnboardingState and not installed until completion screen, so no system changes occur from this screen. Registry caching is in-memory only with no persistent side effects.

completed_when: The Skills Recommendations Screen loads skill data from the remote registry, filters by detected CLIs, supports search and category filtering, allows multi-select checkbox selection, displays Recommended badges, and navigates correctly via Skip and Next buttons with selection state persisted to OnboardingState.
completed_evidence: Screen recording showing registry load, CLI-based filtering with only compatible skills shown, search filtering, category dropdown filtering, multi-skill selection, selection count updating, Next navigation persisting selection. Test report showing all unit and UI tests passing.
dependencies: Requires OnboardingState.detectedCLIs to be populated from CLI Detection screen. Requires OnboardingCoordinator for navigation. Requires network connectivity for registry fetch. SkillsRegistryService is a new component created as part of this atom.
status_reason: Specified and ready for implementation. Depends on CLI Detection screen for detected CLI data. Low risk as this screen has no side effects beyond OnboardingState updates and can be safely skipped if issues arise.
open_questions: What is the production URL for the skills registry endpoint
Should registry include skill file sizes for download estimation
Should we implement local fallback registry bundle for offline scenarios
How frequently should cached registry data be refreshed during a session
notes: This screen is lower stakes than CLI Detection because no system modifications occur. Users can skip entirely or proceed with zero selections. The main risk is registry availability - consider implementing a fallback static bundle if registry proves unreliable. Popularity sorting helps surface quality skills without requiring manual curation of the registry.

risks: Registry endpoint unavailable or returns errors during user onboarding
Registry returns very large response causing memory pressure or slow parse
Network latency causes poor user experience with long loading times
Registry schema changes break client parsing without warning
mitigations: Implement clear error state with retry button and option to skip if registry unavailable
Add response size limit check and paginate or truncate if over threshold
Show skeleton loading state immediately and set 5-second timeout with graceful degradation
Use defensive JSON parsing that handles missing optional fields and logs warnings for schema drift
risk_register.blast_radius: Changes isolated to new Onboarding files only. OnboardingState.selectedSkills is the only shared state modified. No system changes occur from this screen. Skip button provides escape hatch for any issues.
risk_register.fallback_plan: If registry fetch fails repeatedly, show manual skills documentation link and allow user to proceed via Skip. If entire screen proves problematic, set OnboardingState.skipSkillsScreen = true in OnboardingCoordinator to bypass screen in flow.

persistence: OnboardingState.selectedSkills: Set<String> persisted to UserDefaults for installation at completion screen
In-memory registry cache in SkillsRegistryService for session duration (no disk persistence)
